features.name: Vault owner delayed withdrawal
features.proof: Accepted TN12 vault delayed withdrawal transaction
features.risk: Only the delay, owner signature, output value, and owner output script are enforced.
features.nextHardeningStep: Add negative tests for early withdrawal, wrong signer, wrong output, and wrong amount.

features.name: Vault recovery spend
features.risk: Recovery path is immediate in the current primitive.
features.nextHardeningStep: Prototype optional recovery delay or guardian policy as separate explicit script logic.

features.name: Vault daily limit
features.risk: UI could imply a spend cap the contract does not enforce.
features.nextHardeningStep: Either remove from enforced-language copy or add script/indexer design before product claims.

features.name: Vault guardian threshold
features.risk: Guardian counts are design intent, not active covenant logic.
features.nextHardeningStep: Add a separate guardian vault template after key roles and script semantics are clear.

features.name: Individual pledge release
features.risk: The script releases a single pledge to the recipient; it does not verify campaign target reached.
features.nextHardeningStep: Keep UI label as individual pledge primitive until target aggregation has stronger enforcement.

features.name: Individual pledge refund after deadline
features.risk: Refund path is per pledge, not campaign-wide refund batching.
features.nextHardeningStep: Add negative test for refund before deadline and wrong contributor signature.

features.name: Batch assurance target progress
features.risk: Accepted progress is useful app state but not pooled covenant enforcement.
features.nextHardeningStep: Import real accepted pledge outpoints and build release/refund draft planning.

features.name: Invoice paid state
features.proof: Receipt draft exists; accepted payload receipt still gated
features.risk: Invoice must not become paid until an accepted transaction carries the matching payload.
features.nextHardeningStep: Verify a wallet route that preserves payload bytes, then submit one accepted receipt.

features.name: Submit console private-key separation
features.proof: UI reads signed draft artifacts only
features.risk: The safety boundary depends on scripts and file hygiene, not consensus.
features.nextHardeningStep: Add private-key string guards and explicit draft provenance metadata.

features.name: Cross-chain idea mapping
features.risk: Open-source references can be mistaken for Kaspa feature availability.
features.nextHardeningStep: Keep every app brief tied to live Kaspa, TN12/Toccata, roadmap, or research status.

features.name: Escrow spend paths
features.currentSurface: contracts/Escrow.sil, contracts/EscrowExpired.sil, fixtures/EscrowContractOutpoint.json, fixtures/EscrowDaaRefundContractOutpoint.json, signed escrow funding/release/refund/cancel drafts, and browser escrow panel
features.proof: Accepted escrow release spend, accepted DAA-expired escrow refund spend, and accepted mutual-cancel spend on separate P2SH outputs.
features.risk: Release, refund, and cancel are mutually exclusive spends of one escrow output, so proof paths must continue using separate funded outputs.
features.nextHardeningStep: Add negative tests around v1 computeBudget preservation and keep the local TN12 SDK route documented.

features.name: Treasury payroll and spend caps
features.risk: Payroll templates and spend caps are review policy until script or indexer enforcement exists.
features.nextHardeningStep: Build constrained team spend drafts, add exact UTXO provenance, and separate role keys.

features.name: Coordination-market Hunt execution
features.proof: Generated transparent toy solver artifact only
features.risk: Transparent satisfiable packs are not opaque accumulation, capital multiplexing, composability, or coordinated atomic execution.
features.nextHardeningStep: Build exact settlement drafts for one satisfiable transparent pack before claiming any Hunt execution proof.

features.name: Access pass redemption
features.currentSurface: fixtures/AccessPassPlanner.json and browser access pass panel
features.proof: Generated access pass planner artifact only
features.risk: Issuer-backed redemption state can be useful, but it is not native ticket enforcement.
features.nextHardeningStep: Tie one redemption to an accepted payload receipt and add duplicate redemption checks.

features.name: Simple asset policy
features.currentSurface: fixtures/SimpleAssetPolicies.json and browser asset policy panel
features.risk: Issuer-indexed assets and future covenant-native assets can be confused if not labeled.
features.nextHardeningStep: Tie issuer-indexed asset state to accepted payload receipts and keep covenant-native rules roadmap-only.

features.name: Auction intent winner selection
features.risk: Accepted bid payload ranking is useful app state, but it is not atomic exchange, bid custody, or MEV-resistant settlement.
features.nextHardeningStep: Build explicit settlement/refund drafts and keep winner selection labeled as planner/indexer state.

features.name: DeFi research backlog
features.currentSurface: fixtures/DefiResearchBacklog.json, fixtures/StableValuePaths.json, fixtures/StableIssuerRedemptions.json, and browser DeFi panel
features.proof: Generated DeFi backlog, stable-value comparison, and issuer redemption-state artifacts only
features.risk: Research briefs can be mistaken for live swaps, lending, stable-value products, native stablecoins, insurance, or derivatives.
features.nextHardeningStep: Build simulation-only dashboards and missing-rails checklists before any settlement prototype.

features.name: AI-agent commitment settlement
features.risk: Accepted task/proof/dispute payloads are app state, not autonomous payout authorization or objective proof of completion.
features.nextHardeningStep: Build exact release/refund drafts and require wallet review before any submit path.

rules: A browser feature is not a contract guarantee unless this matrix says enforcement is script.
Planner/indexer state can make app UX useful, but it must not be described as covenant-enforced.
Wallet policy is a safety layer, not consensus enforcement.
Simulation-only features stay product direction until a script, accepted indexer, or wallet route proves them.
